summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Pennsylvania - Title 23 Pa.C.S. Chapter 63 (Child Protective Services Law)
Pennsylvania - 42 Pa.C.S. Chapter 63 (Juvenile Act – dependency proceedings)
Title 23: Domestic Relations - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the Superior Court and reinstated the trial court's denial of a goal change, holding that dependency rulings are reviewed only for abuse of discretion and that fifteen months in placement under 42 Pa.C.S. § 6351(f)(9) is one factor, not a litmus test requiring a goal change.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms that reunification may remain the goal even after long placement if the trial court's findings support it.
key_cases.quote: (f)(9) is merely one of a number of factors a trial court must consider in ultimately determining whether the current placement is appropriate

key_cases.holding: Reversing the Superior Court and reinstating termination, the court held that an agency's failure to provide reasonable efforts toward reunification does not bar the granting of an otherwise properly proven petition to terminate parental rights, although courts may enforce reasonable efforts by other means.
key_cases.relevance: Marks the point at which reunification ceases to be a realistic goal despite deficient agency efforts.
key_cases.quote: refusing a properly proven termination of parental rights petition, and thus harming an innocent child, is not among them

key_cases.holding: Affirming the Superior Court, the court held that a court-ordered change of the permanency goal is not a condition precedent to an agency's filing of a petition to terminate parental rights, consistent with ASFA's endorsement of concurrent planning.
key_cases.relevance: Reunification can remain the stated goal while the agency pursues an alternative permanency track.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that Section 6351 does not require that a goal change precede the filing of a termination petition.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed and ordered termination of parental rights for five siblings, holding that under 23 Pa.C.S. § 2511(b) an unhealthy or pathological parent-child bond does not preclude termination and that courts must weigh the child's need for permanency and any bond with a pre-adoptive family.
key_cases.relevance: Identifies when reunification must yield because the parent cannot parent within a reasonable period.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that severing the parental bond best serves the needs and welfare of these children

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the Superior Court, holding that a child whose non-custodial parent is ready, willing and able to provide proper care does not meet the Juvenile Act definition of a dependent child and may not be adjudicated dependent.
key_cases.relevance: Placement with the capable non-custodial parent, not dependency, is the correct outcome.
key_cases.quote: a child is not dependent if the child has a parent who is willing and able to provide proper care to the child

state_agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Office of Children, Youth, and Families

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21, conditional: adjudicated dependent before 18, youth requests the court to retain jurisdiction, and meets one of five activity conditions; re-entry may be requested before 21 (42 Pa.C.S. §§ 6302, 6351(j))

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
